stem: A Zero Trust program verifies every sign-in, yet many accounts still hold standing full-access roles. Which Zero Trust principle is missing?

choices.text: Use least-privilege access so identities receive only the permissions required for the task
Trust any later request that originates on the corporate LAN
Treat the first successful VPN connection as permanent authorization
Replace identity verification with a single inbound allow-all network rule

explanation: Zero Trust includes least privilege. Verifying sign-ins is incomplete if identities keep standing full access after authentication.

source.title: Zero Trust as a security foundation

stem: Which two principles are core to a Zero Trust architecture? (Choose two.)

choices.text: Verify explicitly
Use least-privilege access
Trust all internal network traffic by default
Disable continuous validation after the first successful sign-in

explanation: Microsoft describes Zero Trust around verify explicitly, least privilege, and assume breach. Default internal trust and one-time validation contradict that model.

stem: A user completes password and MFA challenges. Only afterward does the app decide whether that account may open a finance report. Which statement is accurate?

choices.text: Authorization happened first and made authentication unnecessary
Successful authentication automatically authorizes every Microsoft 365 action
Authentication proved who the user is; authorization then decided what the identity may do
The report permission check is a Conditional Access named-location signal, not authorization

explanation: Authentication verifies identity first. Authorization is the later permission decision and is not implied by a successful sign-in.

stem: Which grouping correctly describes common authentication factor categories?

choices.text: Retention, deletion, and record declaration
SIEM collection, SOAR automation, and hunting
Sensitivity labeling, DLP blocking, and eDiscovery hold
Something you know, something you have, and something you are

explanation: Authentication factors are commonly knowledge, possession, and inherence. The other groupings are compliance or SOC capabilities, not authentication factor types.

stem: A contractor signs in successfully with MFA but cannot open a payroll app. A colleague says the sign-in proves the contractor is allowed to use every company app. What is wrong with that claim?

choices.text: Authentication success does not grant every permission; authorization still evaluates roles and policies
MFA replaces role-based access control, so the app should open automatically
Federation always grants Global Administrator rights after sign-in
Authorization applies only to guest users and never to contractors who can sign in

explanation: A completed sign-in proves identity. Apps and roles still authorize what that identity may access, so MFA success is not blanket permission.

subobjective: Define identity as the primary security perimeter
stem: Users connect to Microsoft 365 from home networks, coffee shops, and mobile carriers. Security still treats a corporate firewall as the main control that makes those requests safe. Which shift does SC-900 emphasize?

choices.text: Assume any request from a coffee-shop Wi-Fi is trusted if it uses HTTPS
Treat identity and access context as a primary security perimeter rather than relying on a castle-and-moat network
Replace identity verification with Azure Bastion for all SaaS apps
Move all access decisions into records management

explanation: Cloud access from many networks makes identity the primary perimeter. A corporate firewall alone cannot attest who is requesting SaaS access.

stem: A SaaS app is configured to trust Microsoft Entra ID and no longer stores user passwords itself. What is Entra ID acting as for that app?

choices.text: A data loss prevention engine that blocks outbound credit-card numbers
A SIEM that correlates firewall logs
An identity provider that authenticates users and issues trusted tokens or claims
A records-management service that declares contracts as records

explanation: An identity provider authenticates users and issues claims that apps trust, so the app does not need a local password store.

stem: A partner organization authenticates its own employees, then those users access your app through a trust relationship. Which concept is that, and why is it not multifactor authentication?

choices.text: Federation is Microsoft's name for requiring two authentication factors
Federation replaces authorization while MFA replaces authentication
Federation is a Purview audit log, and MFA is a retention label
Federation establishes identity trust and claim exchange between organizations; MFA is a factor-strength requirement during authentication

explanation: Federation is an identity-trust relationship that can accept claims from a partner identity provider. MFA is about using more than one authentication factor, not about org-to-org trust.

subobjective: Describe the concept of directory services and Active Directory
stem: A learner says Active Directory Domain Services is simply another name for Microsoft Entra ID in the cloud. Which correction is accurate?

choices.text: AD DS is the traditional on-premises directory service; Entra ID is Microsoft's cloud identity service and they are not the same thing
AD DS is only a Conditional Access grant control
Entra ID exists only to host Azure Firewall policies
AD DS and Entra ID are both names for Microsoft Defender for Identity

explanation: AD DS remains the on-premises directory. Entra ID is the cloud identity platform. Hybrid identity can connect them, but the services are distinct.

stem: A team must protect customer records while they travel between a browser and a web app. Which cryptographic control is designed for that state of data?

choices.text: Hashing the records so authorized users can decrypt them later
Encryption in transit, such as TLS, to protect data as it moves across the network
A retention label that encrypts packets at the NSG
Privileged Identity Management, which encrypts HTTP bodies

explanation: Data in transit is protected with encryption such as TLS. Hashing is one-way and not a decryptable transport control, and PIM or retention labels are not packet encryption.

stem: Which statement correctly contrasts encryption with hashing?

choices.text: Hashing hides contents for later decryption, while encryption can never be reversed
Encryption and hashing are both names for Conditional Access grant controls
Encryption is designed to be reversed with the correct key; hashing is a one-way fingerprint that should not be decrypted
Hashing is only used to activate privileged roles in PIM

explanation: Encryption supports confidentiality and is reversible with authorized keys. Hashing produces a one-way digest used for integrity, not decryption.

subobjective: Describe Governance, Risk, and Compliance (GRC) concepts
stem: Leadership writes acceptable-use rules, a risk team estimates likely impact of a ransomware event, and auditors later check whether those rules were followed. Which mapping is accurate?

choices.text: Governance is only Microsoft Defender for Endpoint, risk is only Azure WAF, and compliance is only NSGs
Risk management replaces the need for any compliance evidence
Compliance is the product name for Microsoft Sentinel playbooks
Governance sets direction, risk assesses uncertainty, and compliance checks adherence

explanation: GRC separates oversight and policy (governance), uncertainty analysis (risk), and demonstrated adherence (compliance). They are not individual Microsoft security products.

stem: An attacker bypasses a network control but is still stopped by identity MFA and by encryption on the data store. Which security model does that outcome illustrate?

choices.text: Defense-in-depth, because remaining independent layers still contained the failure
A single-perimeter design that depends only on the network control
Federation, because MFA is a partner identity-trust relationship
Records management, because encryption declares a file as a record

explanation: Defense-in-depth expects layers such as identity and data protection to continue working when one layer fails. A single network control would not have stopped the attacker.

stem: In Microsoft's shared responsibility model, which two duties remain with the customer across IaaS, PaaS, and SaaS? (Choose two.)

choices.text: Protecting customer data
Managing identities and access to that data
Physically securing Microsoft datacenter buildings
Operating the underlying public-cloud host hardware

explanation: Customers retain data, identities, and access responsibilities in every cloud model. Physical datacenters and host hardware in the public cloud remain Microsoft's.

source.title: Shared responsibility in the cloud - Microsoft Azure

stem: An organization uses Azure virtual machines in Microsoft's public cloud. Who is typically responsible for physically protecting the datacenter and replacing failed host hardware?

choices.text: The customer, because IaaS transfers datacenter physical security to every tenant
The customer's ISP, which becomes the datacenter operator
Microsoft, as the cloud provider of the physical facility and host infrastructure
Microsoft Purview eDiscovery, which physically guards racks

explanation: In public cloud IaaS, Microsoft still operates physical facilities and host hardware. The customer remains responsible for the guest OS, identities, and data.

source.title: Shared responsibility in the cloud - Microsoft Azure

subobjective: Describe Governance, Risk, and Compliance (GRC) concepts
stem: A regulator asks whether the company followed its stated retention and access policies. Which GRC activity is that request primarily about?

choices.text: Only threat hunting in Microsoft Sentinel
Only issuing a Temporary Access Pass
Only creating an Azure virtual network
Compliance: demonstrating that required policies and controls were actually followed

explanation: Compliance is about showing adherence to obligations and internal policy. Hunting, TAP, and VNets are security or identity capabilities, not the GRC compliance activity itself.

stem: Which statement best describes a Microsoft Entra tenant in SC-900 terms?

choices.text: A dedicated cloud identity boundary that represents an organization and holds its directory objects
A DDoS mitigation policy attached to a public IP
A Purview retention label that encrypts packets
A Sentinel playbook that replaces the need for identities

explanation: An Entra tenant is the organization's cloud directory boundary for users, apps, and related identity objects. It is not a network, retention, or SIEM control.

source.title: What is Microsoft Entra? - Microsoft Entra

subobjective: Describe types of identities, including agent ID
stem: A supplier's employees must sign in to a procurement app without being created as full internal staff. Which Entra identity approach fits that need?

choices.text: Replacing the app with Azure Key Vault so no sign-in is required
External or guest identities for partner and customer collaboration
Declaring each supplier employee as a retention label
Using Microsoft Defender Vulnerability Management as the identity type

explanation: External/guest identities let partners or customers authenticate without becoming full internal employees. Key Vault, retention labels, and vulnerability management are not identity types.

source.title: Describe the Function and Identity Types of Microsoft Entra ID

stem: An organization keeps on-premises Active Directory and needs those accounts available in Microsoft Entra ID. Which component is the usual synchronization engine for that hybrid identity?

choices.text: Azure Web Application Firewall, which copies users during HTTP inspection
Microsoft Purview Content explorer, which syncs directory objects
Microsoft Entra Connect, which synchronizes on-premises identities to Entra ID
Azure Bastion, which replicates passwords over RDP

explanation: Entra Connect (and related hybrid identity tooling) synchronizes on-premises AD identities to Entra ID. WAF, Content explorer, and Bastion do not perform directory sync.

source.title: What is hybrid identity with Microsoft Entra ID? - Microsoft Entra ID

stem: Which statement correctly distinguishes password hash synchronization from pass-through authentication in hybrid identity?

choices.text: Pass-through authentication stores plaintext passwords in Entra ID while hash sync disables hybrid identity
Both methods are Azure Firewall FQDN rules rather than authentication paths
Password hash synchronization is a Defender XDR workload, and pass-through authentication is a sensitivity label
Password hash synchronization authenticates in the cloud using hashed secrets; pass-through authentication validates passwords against on-premises Active Directory

explanation: PHS enables cloud authentication with hashed password material. PTA sends the validation to on-premises AD. Neither is a firewall or XDR control.

source.title: What is hybrid identity with Microsoft Entra ID? - Microsoft Entra ID

stem: A company wants users to sign in with FIDO2 security keys and Microsoft Authenticator without typing a password. How does that relate to MFA?

choices.text: Passwordless methods can still satisfy strong multifactor or phishing-resistant authentication without using a password as a factor
Passwordless sign-in is the same as disabling MFA permanently
FIDO2 keys are retention labels and cannot participate in authentication
Authenticator without a password is only a Service Trust Portal offering

explanation: Passwordless methods such as FIDO2 and Authenticator still use strong factors. They are not a way to turn MFA off, and they are not compliance-portal artifacts.

source.title: Microsoft Entra multifactor authentication overview - Microsoft Entra ID

subobjective: Describe password protection and management capabilities
stem: Helpdesk wants users to reset forgotten passwords themselves after extra verification. Security also wants to block passwords that contain the company name. Which pairing is accurate?

choices.text: Self-service password reset is the banned-password dictionary, and password protection is eDiscovery hold
Self-service password reset addresses forgotten-password recovery; password protection bans weak or custom banned terms
Both needs are met only by Azure DDoS Protection
Password protection recertifies guest group membership, while SSPR is a WAF policy

explanation: SSPR is recovery after the user proves alternative authentication. Password protection blocks globally banned and custom weak terms. They are related password capabilities, not the same control.

source.title: Self-service password reset deep dive - Microsoft Entra ID

stem: Finance users may open a payroll app from the headquarters network without extra MFA, but the same users must complete MFA from any other network. Which Conditional Access signal supports that difference?

choices.text: A retention label that changes based on the user's GPS coordinates
Azure Bastion, which classifies every public IP as trusted
Named or trusted network locations used as a condition in the policy
Insider Risk Management, which is the grant control for named locations

explanation: Conditional Access can use named or trusted locations as a condition and then require MFA or allow access. Retention labels, Bastion, and Insider Risk Management do not supply that location signal.

source.title: Microsoft Entra Conditional Access: Zero Trust Policy Engine - Microsoft Entra ID

stem: Microsoft Entra ID Protection flags one account because leaked credentials appeared in a dump, and flags another sign-in because it came from an anonymized IP. Which distinction is accurate?

choices.text: User risk and sign-in risk are both names for Azure Firewall application rules
Sign-in risk is only used by Purview records management
User risk replaces Conditional Access and cannot be used as a policy condition
User risk describes the user/account, while sign-in risk describes a specific authentication attempt

explanation: ID Protection separates user risk (the identity) from sign-in risk (the attempt). Those signals can feed Conditional Access; they are not firewall or records controls.

source.title: What is Microsoft Entra ID Protection? - Microsoft Entra ID Protection

subobjective: Describe the capabilities of Microsoft Entra Privileged Identity Management
stem: When an engineer activates an eligible privileged role, security wants an extra MFA prompt and a written justification before the role becomes active. Which PIM capability is that?

choices.text: Activation settings that can require multifactor authentication and justification
A retention policy that expires admin tokens after 90 days of SharePoint inactivity
Azure Web Application Firewall, which approves directory roles
Content explorer filtering, which is required to activate Entra roles

explanation: PIM activation can demand extra authentication, justification, and related checks before a privileged role becomes active. Retention, WAF, and Content explorer do not control Entra role activation.

source.title: What is Privileged Identity Management? - Microsoft Entra ID Governance
